catalysts.label: Ni/MgO microkinetic (Takahashi & Fujitani 2016)
catalysts.composition: 30 wt% Ni/MgO, impregnation, calcined 600 degC, 22-42 mesh powder
catalysts.rate_law_text: Elementary steps NH3+s<=>NH3(a) (k1, k-1=k1/K1); NH3(a)+3s->N(a)+3H(a) (k2, irreversible); 2N(a)->N2+2s (k3, irreversible); 2H(a)<=>H2+2s (k4, k-4=k4/K4). r1=k1*(pNH3/ptot)*th_s - k-1*th_NH3; r2=k2*th_NH3*th_s^3; r3=k3*th_N^2; r4=k4*th_H^2 - k-4*(pH2/ptot)*th_s^2; th_s=1-th_NH3-th_N-th_H; QSS r1=r2, r2=2r3, 3r2=2r4; r_NH3 = r2 [mol s-1 g-1]. k_i=A_i exp(-Ea_i/RT), k1=A1 (Ea1=0); K1=A5 exp(-Ea5/RT); K4=A6 exp(-Ea4/RT).
catalysts.pressure_basis: mole fractions p_i/p_total (atm in the source; ratio is unit free)

Ea4.locator: Table 1 (k4; also used for K4, Eq. 25)

validity.note: fit 350-450 degC, X<20 %, 1 atm; validated 500-650 degC at 1 atm (Figs. 1, 3, 5)

catalysts.experimental_basis: Lab fixed-bed quartz reactor, 1 atm, Ar balance, H2 yield by GC-TCD; catalyst mass not reported; SV 15000-30000 h^-1
limitations: Steps 2 and 3 irreversible in the source: rate does not vanish at equilibrium (AmCraX approach factor optional, see below).
Mole-fraction basis: no intrinsic total-pressure dependence; use at 20 bar is an unvalidated extrapolation.
Nomenclature lists T in degC; T in K reproduces Table 2 (used here).
Table 1 reproduces Table 2 at 500 degC only within 2-7 % (paper rounding); not tuned.
amcrax_extensions: [assumption (AmCraX extension)] r_AmCraX = r_published * (1 - Q/Kp),  Q = y_N2^0.5 * y_H2^1.5 * (P/1 bar) / y_NH3,  Kp from amcrax.thermodynamics (default_on=True). The published microkinetic model omits the reverse of steps 2 and 3 (valid at 1 atm, far from equilibrium at the authors' conditions). At 20 bar the cracked gas approaches equilibrium, and an irreversible law would predict conversion above equilibrium. The factor forces r -> 0 at equilibrium; it is switchable (approach_factor=False).

catalysts.label: Ru/MgO microkinetic (Takahashi & Fujitani 2016)
catalysts.composition: 5 wt% Ru/MgO, impregnation (RuCl3), calcined 600 degC, 22-42 mesh powder
catalysts.rate_law_text: Same elementary-step model as ni_takahashi_microkinetic with Ru parameters (Table 1).

validity.note: fit 300-400 degC, X<20 %, 1 atm; validated 450-550 degC at 1 atm (Figs. 2, 4, 5)

catalysts.experimental_basis: Lab fixed-bed quartz reactor, 1 atm, Ar balance; catalyst mass not reported; SV 15000-30000 h^-1
limitations: Steps 2 and 3 irreversible: equilibrium approach factor is an AmCraX extension.
Mole-fraction basis: no total-pressure dependence; 20 bar use is extrapolation.
N2 recombinative desorption is rate limiting on Ru (pp. 6-7).
amcrax_extensions: [assumption (AmCraX extension)] r_AmCraX = r_published * (1 - Q/Kp),  Q = y_N2^0.5 * y_H2^1.5 * (P/1 bar) / y_NH3,  Kp from amcrax.thermodynamics (default_on=True). The published microkinetic model omits the reverse of steps 2 and 3 (valid at 1 atm, far from equilibrium at the authors' conditions). At 20 bar the cracked gas approaches equilibrium, and an irreversible law would predict conversion above equilibrium. The factor forces r -> 0 at equilibrium; it is switchable (approach_factor=False).

catalysts.label: Ru/Al2O3 Temkin-Pyzhev (Kum et al. 2026, fit to Di Carlo et al. 2014)
catalysts.rate_law_text: r = ko*exp(-Ea/(R*T)) * [ (P_NH3^2/P_H2^3)^beta - (P_N2/Keq^2)*(P_H2^3/P_NH3^2)^(1-beta) ], P in bar, r in mol g_cat^-1 s^-1 (per mol NH3)

validity.note: fit to 36 points of dicarlo2014ammonia, GHSV 300-2400 h^-1, MAPE 0.81 % (p. 9); source applies it up to 773 K / 13 bar

catalysts.experimental_basis: Kinetic fit by kum2026heatintegrated to experimental data of dicarlo2014ammonia (commercial Ru/Al2O3)
limitations: Keq basis ambiguous in the source; AmCraX reading is an assumption (see equilibrium_constant).
Extrapolation above 723 K and above 10 bar is unvalidated.
Rate is singular at P_H2 -> 0; the PFR starts from a small H2 seed (numerical assumption).
Nomenclature lists R in m3 bar/(mol K); J/(mol K) is required because Ea is in J/mol.
amcrax_extensions: [assumption] dGr is read as J per 2 mol NH3 (2NH3 -> N2 + 3H2), verified against Cantera gri30 to <0.5 kJ (research synthesis check). The driving force of Eq. 2 vanishes at equilibrium only if Keq^2 = exp(-dGr/RT) (Keq per mol NH3, 1 bar standard state). AmCraX therefore uses Keq^2 = exp(-dGr/(R*T)).

equilibrium_constant.published: Keq = exp(-dGr/(R*T)); dGr = 95117 - 193.67*T - 0.035293*T^2 + 9.22e-6*T^3 (Eqs. 3-4, p. 4; unit of dGr not printed)
equilibrium_constant.assumption_text: dGr is read as J per 2 mol NH3 (2NH3 -> N2 + 3H2), verified against Cantera gri30 to <0.5 kJ (research synthesis check). The driving force of Eq. 2 vanishes at equilibrium only if Keq^2 = exp(-dGr/RT) (Keq per mol NH3, 1 bar standard state). AmCraX therefore uses Keq^2 = exp(-dGr/(R*T)).
equilibrium_constant.options: keq_basis='published' (Eq. 4 with the above reading) or 'amcrax_thermo' (Kp from amcrax.thermodynamics, NASA7/GRI-Mech 3.0)

rho_cat_kg_m3.locator: Table 1; used as (1-eps_b)*rho_cat in Table 2 mass balance, i.e. particle density

notes: Rate laws are literature models (see each source citation); validity ranges and limitations are listed per catalyst.
Evaluating them at conditions outside the validity range is an extrapolation and is labelled python_model.
